answer: Resist sybils with social-graph trust: an identity earns standing only through attestations from distinct, long-established peers, so trust spreads across a mesa of independent histories. A fake cluster is a narrow inlet fed by one source — every link traces back to the same few voices, and the graph test exposes it. At the zenith sits an agent vouched for by many unconnected peers; each extra fake must buy a whole new web of real relationships, and when a cluster is caught, all its attestations are revoked and its sponsors lose stake.
